scope: Historical source audit for the reported pure-state exclusions N=9,t=3 and N=10,t=4.
result: No explicit global exclusion proof or machine-checkable certificate located in the primary literature examined. This is a research-search result, not a claim that no proof exists anywhere.

sources.title: Optimal Detection of Rotations about Unknown Axes by Coherent and Anticoherent States
sources.finding: Explicitly states absence of orders t>=3 for j=9/2 and t>=4 for j=5. These sections do not give exclusion proofs, algebraic certificates, or case-specific proof references. They provide lower-order witnesses and numerical optimization discussion.
sources.interpretation: Appropriate provenance for 'reported absent'; the categorical wording alone does not establish a reproducible proof in this catalogue.

sources.title: Extremal quantum states and their Majorana constellations
locations: Table I caption and j=9/2,j=5 rows, PDFp3
sources.quote: which we conjecture is the highest possible
sources.finding: Describes solving real quadratic multipole equations using MAGMA Gröbner bases, including the ability to detect infeasibility. Crucially, Table I explicitly labels its listed highest orders conjectural. Rows j=9/2 and j=5 give orders 2 and 3. The generic computational-method sentence cannot be promoted into a case-specific exclusion certificate.
sources.interpretation: Independent primary-source evidence that these maximal-order claims were conjectural in the 2015 work cited by Quantum2020.

sources.title: Stars of the quantum Universe: extremal constellations on the Poincaré sphere
sources.quote: we conjecture that no third-order unpolarized constellations exist
sources.finding: Explicitly calls absence of third-order anticoherence at spin9/2 a conjecture. Earlier on printed p4 the authors explain that their Gröbner-based approach has not supplied a general assurance of finding all constellations or the highest attainable order. The PDF includes a cover sheet, so PDF page numbers are one larger than printed page numbers.
sources.interpretation: The clearest primary statement of the historical status of N9,t3.

sources.title: Anticoherence measures for pure spin states
sources.finding: Search-derived occurrence diagram. Missing blocks reflect absence of convergence to AC states, not a proof of nonexistence. This does not independently resolve the two target cells.

sources.title: Library of spin anticoherent states
sources.author: John Martin
sources.finding: Lists witnesses of orders2 and3 for N9 andN10. Its discussion explicitly treats equality between maximum AC order and spherical-design degree as conjectural; the Majorana-constellation iff-design conjecture is already false. Therefore nonexistence results for spherical designs do not prove the target AC exclusions.

negativeSearchResults.certificate: No case-specific certificate or public exact elimination output located.
negativeSearchResults.grasslDatabase: The referenced polarization.markus-grassl.de site did not load through the browser tool; no inference about unpublished code or data is made.
negativeSearchResults.sphericalDesignShortcut: Invalid without a further theorem relating existence of AC states to existence of spherical designs.

suggestedCatalogueWording: Reported absent in Quantum 4,285 (2020). The earlier primary sources explicitly classified the relevant maximal-order claims as conjectural; no explicit exclusion certificate has been reproduced here.

catalogueFollowup.result: Both exclusions are now independently proved by exact catalogue certificates; no external source is used as proof of the new identities.
catalogueFollowup.additionalResult: The previously unresolved N=11,t=4 case is independently excluded by two exact three-copy certificates; this completes the n=2–12 core.
